subject: general
question: Which act stated that the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay were to be subordinate to the Presidency of Bengal in all matters of war, diplomatic relations and revenue?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pitts' India Act, 1784**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pitts' India Act, 1784 was enacted to bring more control and accountability in the administration of British territories in India.
 
• It established a system where the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay were made subordinate to the Presidency of Bengal in all matters concerning war, diplomacy, and revenue.
 
• The act created a dual system of governance where the British Crown and the East India Company shared authority over Indian administration.
 
• A Board of Control was set up to oversee political affairs, while the Court of Directors retained control over commercial activities.
 
• It marked a significant step towards centralized governance in British India under the Presidency of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Presidency System:** British India was divided into three presidencies—Bengal, Madras, and Bombay—each governed by its own administration.
 
• **Board of Control:** Established by Pitts' India Act, it consisted of six members, including the British Cabinet Ministers, to oversee political governance in India.
 
• **Dual System of Governance:** Authority over India was shared between the Crown (through the Board of Control) and the East India Company (through the Court of Directors).
 
• **Revenue Administration:** Subordination of Madras and Bombay to Bengal helped establish a centralized mechanism for managing revenue collection and financial affairs.
 
• **Impact of the Act:** It strengthened British control over India and laid the foundation for future legislative acts aimed at consolidating imperial governance.
